name: exploit
cleaning_prompt:
DATASET: U.S. weekly ILI-ratio panel. Clean ONLY the current row's week (exact calendar week).

ROLE: Place THIS week in its flu-season regime, then list only this-week shocks with direct ILI impact. Remove all non-ILI content, off-week data, and any text not directly tied to the current week's U.S. surveillance or burden.

FORBIDDEN: year cutoffs; stuffing; header-only shells; inventing. Never keep non-ILI facts (e.g., wellness, foreign outbreaks, vaccine research, strain-only data, mortality, or historical flu) unless they are explicitly linked to ILI reporting or burden THIS week. Never invent ILI percentages or values.

Output structure (omit empty sections; if nothing usable → EMPTY):

## Regime (≤2 bullets): early ascent / peak / decline / inter-season / pandemic-overlap
— must be supported by THIS week's source, not prior knowledge alone.

## This-week shocks (primary): FluView/ILI, severity, strain, school — dated ±14 days.
— include only events with direct ILI impact (e.g., ILI% change, strain shift, hospitalizations, school closures, regional outbreaks).

## Official prints: exact ILI% / visit / death figures when present.
— only if sourced from THIS week’s CDC/FluView/ILINet or equivalent.

## Likely noise: foreign, wellness, off-week recycle (≤3, optional).
— list only if they are clearly off-topic or misaligned; otherwise drop.

COVID-era rows: KEEP COVID text only when it clearly affects ILI reporting or respiratory co-circulation THIS week; otherwise drop.

NO GLOBAL YEAR CUTOFF: never discard pre-2020 or post-2024 data unless the event year is ≥2 years off the row year. Keep on-year U.S. drivers even if the paragraph contains off-year noise — strip the noise, keep the driver.

NO DATE STUFFING: never copy a recent release (e.g., 2024 BLS/EIA) into old rows. If the row’s source text is empty/NA/useless, output EMPTY.

NO HEADER-ONLY SHELLS: do not emit section titles with no facts.

DATE ALIGNMENT (HARD): keep a fact only if its printed event/release date is within ±14 days of the ROW week (prefer same MMWR week). Drop bullets whose year is off by ≥2 years, and drop recycled encyclopedia blocks that mix many distant years.

NO OVER-DELETE: empty output is allowed only when THIS row's source has no usable on-period U.S. driver after stripping noise. If a clear on-period U.S. surveillance print remains, KEEP it.

PANEL CONTEXT: US_FLURATIO_Week is a LONG weekly U.S. ILI-ratio panel (~1997-09 → 2024-05). Raw Final_Search_4 is often noisy with CDC FluView, state health notes, foreign outbreaks, COVID essays, and recycled flu history. Clean EACH row for THAT week’s calendar date only. Target series = U.S. outpatient ILI ratio / FluView-like burden — NOT generic "health news", NOT COVID hospitalization alone unless it clearly distorts ILI reporting that week. PAST FAILURE MODES TO AVOID: global year cutoffs; stuffing recent FluView into old weeks; header-only empty shells; inventing ILI%; wiping a week that still has a usable on-week U.S. surveillance print; keeping only encyclopedia flu history with no week-local signal.

KEEP (rigorous): CDC FluView / ILINet ILI%; weighted ILI; outpatient visits; flu+ hospital admissions / pediatric deaths when dated; dominant strain (H1N1/H3N2/B) shifts; vaccine coverage or vaccine-effectiveness notes for the current season; school openings/closures or holiday travel explicitly linked to ILI; state/regional outbreaks that can move the national ILI residual.

DROP: wellness blogs; foreign-only outbreaks with no U.S. ILI link; ads; pure COVID policy opinion without ILI reporting impact; far-misaligned recycled pandemic essays; lab-method tutorials; single-clinic anecdotes.

Empty/NA/useless after stripping → empty. Never invent %. Prefer short dense dated lines over wipe-or-stuff extremes.
